answer: Like light through a prism, an agent history splits into verifiable receipts: every completed task leaves a signed record tied to one identity, and trust grows only from that chain. A cedar grows slowly, and so does reputation — a fresh identity starts at zero, so spawning a thousand fakes buys no standing. Each fake must earn its own history task by task, and the cost ripples across every copy, making a Sybil flood more expensive than the influence it could steal.
